notes: Millage is dollars per $1,000 of taxable value: tax = taxable value / 1000 x millage, summed over every levy in the parcel's tax district.

Taxable value is assessed value minus exemptions. The first $25,000 homestead exemption applies to all levies. The second $25,000 homestead exemption (on assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000) does NOT apply to school levies. So for a homestead, the school taxable value can be up to $25,000 higher than the county, city, and other taxable value. A calculator needs two taxable values.
Save Our Homes caps annual growth in homestead assessed value (3% or CPI, whichever is lower) for all levies. The 10% non-homestead assessment cap applies to non-school levies only.

Bay District School Board levies are split into Required Local Effort (set by the state each year through the FEFP), Discretionary Operating (0.748) and Local Capital Improvement (1.500). There was no voted or debt-service school millage in 2020-2025. DOR's TACD and the Tax Collector publish discretionary plus capital outlay as one 'School Discretionary' figure of 2.2480.
The county fire MSTU (1.38) applies only in unincorporated Bay County (TACD districts 55 and 56). Cities provide their own fire service, often funded by non-ad valorem fire assessments.

Mosquito control is split. County Mosquito Control (0.20, county-dependent) applies everywhere except Panama City Beach and the unincorporated beach area. Those two areas pay the independent Beach Mosquito Control District rate instead.
Panama City Beach levies no city ad valorem millage. It funds services through non-ad valorem fire, stormwater, and CRA assessments, plus other revenue.
City of Parker had no city millage in 2020-2022. It began levying 3.0000 mills in tax year 2023.
Bay County BOCC raised countywide operating millage from 4.4362 to 5.4362 in tax year 2023 (FY2024), 34.3% above the rolled-back rate.
No city or county ad valorem debt-service (voted bond) millage appears for any Bay authority in 2020-2025 (DOR databook debt-service columns are blank; the 2025 TACD debt columns are 0.0000).
Panama City Downtown Improvement Board (3.0 mills) applies only to downtown parcels in TACD district 31 (412 parcels in 2025), on top of Panama City's rate.

Levy figures are DOR 'taxes levied' at the adopted rate as certified for that year. DOR's following-year Table 1 shows slightly different 'prior year' amounts after roll corrections. Example: BOCC 2024 levy is $161,094,369 in the 2024 table and $160,866,813 in the 2025 table. Taxable values are the DOR Databook figures for the year (status R-NVAB for county and school). The FLDOE school budget uses a slightly different certified school taxable value: $34,920,695,024 for 2025, against $35,062,478,679 in the DOR databook.

Cross-check of 2025 rates: DOR Table 1, DOR 2025 TACD, DOR 2025 Max Millage Compliance, and the Bay County Tax Collector 2025 millage list all agree on every authority. NWFWMD's own FY2025-26 hearing document and FLDOE's Bay budget summary confirm 0.0207 and the 3.089/0.748/1.5 school split. The only presentation difference is that the Tax Collector and TACD combine school discretionary and capital as 2.2480.
Mexico Beach (2021) and Panama City (2020) adopted rates below the rolled-back rate. Beach Mosquito Control District adopted below rolled-back in every year, and Panama City DIB in 2025.

Exemptions for seniors, veterans, widows and others vary by levy and city. Bills also carry non-ad valorem assessments, which are separate from millage. Florida offers early-payment discounts: 4% in November, declining monthly.
gaps: School rolled-back rates were not found as published figures for any year. A 2025 news report says the 5.337 adopted rate was 0.99% over rolled-back but gives no figure.

School levy dollars by component (RLE, discretionary, capital) were not found as published DOR figures. Only the total school levy from the DOR databook is given. FLDOE's budget summary lists rates and certified taxable value, so components can be computed but are left null here.
2020 and 2022 school discretionary/capital split is inferred from the combined 2.2480 published in the TACD. FLDOE budget summaries for FY2020-21 and FY2022-23 could not be fetched.

Taxable values for the fire MSTU, county mosquito control, Beach Mosquito Control District, Panama City DIB, and City of Parker were not found as published figures. They are not in the DOR municipal report (Parker is missing from it). They could be derived as levy / millage x 1000.

NWFWMD Bay-specific levy is taken from the DOR databook 'countywide independent special districts' column. NWFWMD is the only countywide independent district in Bay, but DOR does not label it by name.
Bay County Property Appraiser (baypa.net) millage tables and official TRIM / adopted-millage resolutions were not retrieved. Cross-checks used the Tax Collector page and the DOR datasets instead.

Per-parcel non-ad valorem amounts are incomplete. Missing: county solid waste and any county fire assessment rates, the Panama City fire protection assessment rate, and assessments for Callaway, Springfield, Parker and Mexico Beach. Only DOR's FY2025-26 aggregate NAV totals, the PCB FY2025-26 proposed rates, and the Lynn Haven stormwater tiers were captured. NAV aggregates for 2020-2024 exist in the DOR 'Non-Ad Valorem Reports' folders but were not extracted.
Tax year 2026 (FY2027) rates were not collected; they were outside scope.
